identity.title: DEBATE: Would God Allow Evil? @CosmicSkeptic vs @InspiringPhilosophy

identity.speakerIdentityBasis: The moderator names Michael Jones and Alex O’Connor, introduces their positions, and hands the first opening to Michael. Explicit transitions, direct address, and coherent turns identify the advocates. Alex thanks Cameron by name within the excluded coaching response.

nonPrimarySpeakers.name: Cameron Bertuzzi
nonPrimarySpeakers.role: Moderator with one bounded coaching intervention

excludedIntervals.speaker: Cameron Bertuzzi
excludedIntervals.summary: Cameron supplies an internal-consistency reply: Christianity retains a loving God even without objective morality. Overlapping caption events at both handoffs make word-level separation unreliable, so the complete continuous coaching exchange is conservatively counted as host advocacy.
excludedIntervals.burdenImpactRationale: This prompts only the internal-critique line Alex independently develops at 21:02–21:28, 22:50–23:16, and 1:44:57–1:45:47: suffering can challenge a professedly loving God without external moral realism. It introduces neither a new side nor a unique motion burden.

excludedIntervals.speaker: Alex O'Connor
excludedIntervals.summary: Alex directly accepts Cameron’s suggestion, reformulates the loving-God and child-cancer objection, and thanks Cameron by name. The overlapping caption handoff and final transition are included conservatively.
excludedIntervals.burdenImpactRationale: No part of this directly dependent reply is credited or penalized. Alex’s independently delivered opening and immediately preceding consistency argument remain available outside the exclusion; the prompted restatement contributes no separate assessment evidence.

participants.basis: Exactly two primary opponents carry the motion. One bounded host coaching exchange repeats Alex’s independently developed internal-consistency line and is fully excluded together with its dependent reply. Other host turns manage timing, read or clarify audience questions, or give off-motion welfare guidance; they do not advocate an additional motion argument.

format.motionInterpretation: Jones defends consistency and eventual overcoming of suffering within the complete Christian worldview; O’Connor advances an evidential challenge to a loving God, not a proof of logical impossibility. Preserve their dispute over necessity versus defeat of gratuitous suffering, intrinsic versus remedial virtue, natural and animal suffering, selective intervention, parental knowledge, and internal moral critique.
format.offMotionCoverage: Opening logistics, promotion, and outro are not moves. Personal welfare counseling at 1:49:48–1:50:52 and 1:55:41–1:59:20 is peripheral to the motion and is not selected or reproduced as advice for either side. Independently argued points about hope versus truth at 1:40:19–1:42:37 and suffering/virtue elsewhere remain eligible. Audience questions themselves are not credited to either speaker.
